action: The introductory slide lays out the chapter's UV fundamentals and model-unwrapping topics.
view: agenda slide
why: Introduce the chapter before practical work.

action: The agenda adds UV considerations and a character-unwrapping demonstration.
view: agenda slide
why: Outline the practical sequence.

action: A slide compares flat shirt pattern pieces with an assembled shirt.
view: shirt pattern diagram
why: Relate surface unwrapping to the construction of clothing.

action: A diagram highlights garment seam lines before moving to UV design considerations.
view: shirt diagram
why: Show where a surface can be cut into flatter pieces.

action: The artist turns off individual garment and boot wireframe displays in Object Properties.
view: Object Mode, front-facing perspective
why: Clear the clothing overlays before UV work.
reader_equivalent: Set obj.show_wire = False for each affected object.

action: The artist reviews the character and the three-item UV checklist while selecting scene objects.
view: Object Mode, front-facing perspective
why: Organize seam cutting, stretch correction, and UV arrangement.

action: The artist adjusts the viewport focal length while the body is displayed in the UV Editing workspace.
view: Edit Mode, front-facing user perspective with UV Editor alongside
why: Make the character easier to view before cutting seams.

action: The isolated body is inspected near the hip and Live Unwrap is enabled in the 3D viewport options.
view: Edit Mode, local user perspective, UV Editor at left
why: Update the UV layout as seams are marked.

action: The artist reselects the leg-root and ankle loops while looking at the updated UV layout.
tool: edge loop selection and UV Editor
view: Edit Mode, local perspective, front and three-quarter views
why: Prepare the leg ring selections for mirroring.

action: The artist mirrors the leg-loop selection across X and enables Extend in the operator panel.
view: Edit Mode, local front-facing perspective
why: Retain both original and mirrored edge selections for seam marking.

action: The artist inspects mirrored seam rings at the hips and demonstrates selection mirroring on a small region.
view: Edit Mode, local front-facing hip close-up
why: Explain that asymmetric mesh geometry may prevent a matching selection.

action: The artist mirrors an inner-leg edge path and opens Mark Seam while the first leg island is visible.
tool: Select Mirror and Edge > Mark Seam
view: Edit Mode, local rear leg view and UV Editor
why: Open both leg tubes along their inner sides.

action: The artist selects and mirrors the shoulder-side arm loop.
tool: edge loop selection and Select Mirror
view: Edit Mode, local oblique upper-body view
why: Prepare corresponding arm-root seams.

action: The artist mirrors and marks the underside arm path, then checks the paired arm islands and seams.
tool: Select Mirror and Edge > Mark Seam
view: Edit Mode, back, front and side perspective
why: Open the arm tubes with the cut on their less-visible undersides.

action: The artist selects a loop at the neck base and marks it as a seam.
tool: edge loop selection and Mark Seam
view: Edit Mode, local neck close-ups from front and back
why: Separate the neck at a location expected to be covered by clothing.

action: The artist checks the neck island and zooms out to review body seams before moving to the feet.
view: Edit Mode, rear neck close-up then full front perspective
why: Confirm that the neck and limb tubes have opened.
reader_equivalent: Inspect marked edges and the UV islands after unwrap([body]).

action: The artist marks the low perimeter of one foot, mirrors it, and marks the other foot.
tool: Select Mirror and Edge > Mark Seam
view: Edit Mode, local oblique feet close-up
why: Separate the upper foot surface from the sole.

action: The artist selects a linked foot-top UV island to identify its corresponding mesh region.
view: Edit Mode, side view of feet and UV island close-up
why: Check which island belongs to the top of the foot.
reader_equivalent: Inspect UV island membership and corresponding body faces.

action: The artist moves from the completed feet to a close view of the hand and its wrist seam.
view: Edit Mode, local oblique hand close-up
why: Prepare a perimeter cut to separate palm and back of hand.
reader_equivalent: Select a hand perimeter path between wrist seam endpoints.

action: The artist mirrors and marks the hand perimeter, then zooms into its hand-shaped UV island.
tool: Select Mirror, Mark Seam and UV Editor
view: Edit Mode, oblique hand and UV close-up
why: Split hand surfaces and examine the resulting layout before optional finger cuts.

action: The artist mirrors and marks selected finger-base edges and checks the resulting separated UV pieces.
tool: Select Mirror and Edge > Mark Seam
view: Edit Mode, hand close-up and UV Editor
why: Separate fingers from the palm for independent islands.
reader_equivalent: Mark mirrored finger-base seam loops and unwrap([body]).

action: The artist inspects the individual finger islands, reveals hidden geometry, and returns to the full body.
view: Edit Mode, enlarged UV layout then front body perspective
why: Verify finger separation and restore geometry before continuing.

action: The artist marks a side torso path from the armpit toward the leg root and mirrors the selection.
tool: edge path selection, Mark Seam and Select Mirror
view: Edit Mode, local side and back three-quarter torso views
why: Start dividing the torso into front and back surfaces.

action: The artist examines the still-connected torso UV and selects a shoulder connection to split it further.
view: Edit Mode, front, side and shoulder close-up
why: Reduce the torso island's distortion and separate its front from its back.

action: The artist mirrors and marks the shoulder seam and notices the torso islands remain joined at the bottom.
tool: Select Mirror, Mark Seam and UV Editor
view: Edit Mode, shoulder close-up and rear perspective
why: Finish dividing the torso along its upper edge and locate the remaining connection.
reader_equivalent: Mark both shoulder paths and inspect the torso UV layout.

action: The artist selects and marks the short edge span between the legs.
view: Edit Mode, crotch close-up and UV Editor
why: Break the remaining connection between front and back torso islands.

action: The artist selects each torso island to inspect the separate front and back, then turns toward the head.
view: Edit Mode, enlarged UV layout then full body and side head
why: Verify the torso split before moving on.
reader_equivalent: Inspect UV island membership and the corresponding mesh faces.

action: The artist marks mirrored seams around the ear attachments and selects a path up the back of the head.
tool: Select Mirror, Mark Seam and edge path selection
view: Edit Mode, side head then back head close-up
why: Separate the ears and prepare an additional cut to open the distorted head UV.
reader_equivalent: Mark ear attachment loops and select a back-of-head seam path.

action: The artist selects a central path across the rear scalp while orbiting around the head.
view: Edit Mode, rear and overhead head perspective
why: Place the opening cut where hair will conceal it.

action: The artist marks the selected scalp edges and examines the resulting face and head UV shape.
tool: Edge > Mark Seam and UV Editor
view: Edit Mode, front and side head close-ups with UV layout
why: Open the head surface while keeping the cut under the hair.
reader_equivalent: Mark the selected scalp paths and unwrap([body]).

action: Marks the eyelid-rim loop as a seam through the Ctrl+E Edge menu, mirrors the selection with Shift+Ctrl+M (status bar reads 20 edges mirrored), then turns to the inside of the mouth and toggles X-ray with Alt+Z while looking for the lip loop.
tool: Edit Mode, Edge select; Edge menu > Mark Seam; Select Mirror
view: UV Editing workspace: UV editor left, 3D view right; perspective close-up of the eye and side of the face, X-ray on for the mouth
why: Give the eye socket lining and the mouth bag their own islands so they stop distorting the face island.
reader_equivalent: seam_loop(body, <point on eyelid rim>, <direction along rim>, mirror_x=True); toggle X-ray only if you capture the result

action: Finds the first mouth-bag seam too visible from the front, selects a loop one row further inside the lips, marks it with Ctrl+E > Mark Seam, and checks the new island lit orange in the UV editor.
tool: Edit Mode, loop select (Alt+click); Edge menu > Mark Seam
view: 3D view in extreme close-up of the lips (X-ray or inside-the-mouth look), then UV editor zoomed out on the whole layout
why: Hide the seam out of frontal view; the separated mouth bag is then unwrapped on its own.
reader_equivalent: seam_loop(body, <point one loop inside the lip line>, <direction along the lips>, mirror_x=False) then unwrap([body])

action: Hides everything except the head, marks the mouth-bag seam and sees the bag fill the entire UV square; undoes (Ctrl+Z), reveals all with Alt+H and the island returns to its normal small size.
view: UV editor and a perspective view of the head showing the seam as an orange line inside the lips
why: Demonstrates the trap that unwrapping with other faces hidden lets the visible island take the whole square.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.mesh.reveal() before any unwrap; unwrap([body]) over all faces

action: Maximises the UV editor (Ctrl+Space) to inspect the islands, finds the ear island uncomfortable, and in the 3D view selects a ring at the base of the ear plus the ear rim to split it.
tool: UV editor maximised; Edit Mode loop select
view: UV editor full-screen showing the ear islands, then side view of the head with red seam lines at the ear and neck
why: One ear island still looked distorted, so it is cut in two.
reader_equivalent: seam_loop(body, <point on ear base>, <direction>) and seam_loop on the ear rim, mirror_x=True, then unwrap([body])

action: Views the seam lines in front, three-quarter and back views: a line across the top of the head, one down the middle of the back of the skull, a neck ring, and lines down the sides of the torso. Marks the ear seam with Ctrl+E and mirrors with Shift+Ctrl+M (20 edges mirrored).
tool: Edit Mode; Alt-click loop and Pick Shortest Path; Mark Seam; Select Mirror
view: front, three-quarter and back perspective of the head and shoulders
why: Confirm the seams sit where hair or the neck and shoulder lines hide them.
reader_equivalent: seam_loop / seam_path with mirror_x=True; verify via uv_report island count

action: Looks at the finished body UV layout zoomed in, pans over torso, arm, face and ear islands, then steps back to the whole body to check the red seam lines (head, neck, wrists, ankles, crotch).
tool: UV editor maximised (Ctrl+Space), pan and zoom
view: UV editor pan and zoom, then full-body front view of the 3D viewport
why: Quick sanity check that no area is missing a seam or visibly distorted.
reader_equivalent: uv_report(body) island count, then viewport_capture(view='FRONT', frame_object='body_retopo')

action: Presses A in the 3D view so every face is selected and orange in the UV editor, then maximises the UV editor again to see the whole body unwrap as one set of islands.
view: UV Editing workspace; full-body front view; UV editor then maximised
why: Show the unwrap as one sheet before checking it for stretch.

action: Opens the UV editor Overlays popover, turns on UV Stretch with type Angle at opacity 0.5, UV opacity 1.0, edge display Black, and unchecks Faces; the islands turn blue with a few lighter cyan and yellow faces.
view: UV editor maximised, islands at overview and zoomed
why: Read stretch from colour: blue is good, yellow or red is bad.
reader_equivalent: no overlay in headless use; stand in with uv_report(body) stretch_p95 per island

action: Pans around the blue-coloured islands and concludes most are fine; a yellow-green sliver is visible at the very edge of a face fan and the finger tips show light cyan.
view: UV editor overview and zoom plus a 3D view of the head with red seam lines
why: Judge the unwrap by the overall blue tint and treat light patches as small errors to check on the model.

action: Rotates the 3D view around the head and shoulders while still in Edit Mode, with the UV stretch colouring on, before setting up a test texture.
tool: 3D view orbit (Ctrl+Space toggles the editor size)
view: front and three-quarter perspective of the head and chest
why: Preparation for a texture-based stretch test since the overlay alone is not enough.

action: In the Material tab of the Properties editor creates a new material and types the name uv checker; its Principled BSDF shows Base Color white, Metallic 0, Roughness 0.5, IOR 1.5, Alpha 1.
view: front view of head and chest in Edit Mode; Properties editor on the right
why: Needs a material to carry the test image.

action: Opens New Image from the Base Color socket: name uv grid, width and height 4096 px, colour black, Alpha on, 32-bit Float off, Tiled off, Generated Type dropdown (Blank, UV Grid, Color Grid) set to Color Grid; the node then shows the grid image with letter-pair cells.
tool: Properties editor > Base Color > Image Texture > New Image
view: front view of the head; checker letters appear in UV editor
why: A coloured grid with unique letter pairs shows stretch, flips and orientation on the model.

action: Opens the viewport shading popover (Solid mode, Studio lighting) and sets Color to Texture; the body turns multicoloured with letter grid, then closes the image from the UV editor.
tool: 3D view > Viewport Shading popover > Color: Texture
view: front, then side view of the character, Ctrl+Alt used while orbiting
why: See the grid on the model in solid view without switching to Material Preview.

action: Zooms to the face with the checker on; cell sizes differ between cheek and chin, the nose cells are larger, the lips show a distorted grid. The narrator mentions the fist as another bad place.
tool: 3D view zoom with Solid + Color: Texture
view: close-up of face and neck from the front
why: Unequal square size is how stretch is spotted on the model.
reader_equivalent: viewport_capture close-ups of face; compare uv_report px_per_m and stretch_p95

action: Zooms to the feet in the checker view where the squares and letters are slanted, then selects the left foot by hovering and pressing L (select linked) and the foot island highlights in orange in the UV editor.
tool: Edit Mode, L to select linked (hover); view the checker
view: close-ups of the foot, then front view of the whole body with the foot selected
why: Isolate one island to re-unwrap it.
reader_equivalent: select by face_test then unwrap([body]) with MINIMUM_STRETCH

action: With the foot island selected presses U and opens the UV Mapping menu; the first group is Unwrap Angle Based, Unwrap Conformal, Unwrap Minimum Stretch, followed by Smart UV Project, Lightmap Pack, Follow Active Quads, Cube/Cylinder/Sphere Projection, Project from View, Mark Seam, Clear Seam, Reset; the pointer rests on Minimum Stretch.
tool: 3D view > U menu > Unwrap Minimum Stretch
view: foot from the front and below, UV editor on the left
why: Minimum Stretch is the option chosen to relax distorted islands.

action: With all faces selected opens the UV editor UV menu and picks Average Islands Scale (the menu also lists Live Unwrap ticked, Pack Islands, Minimize Stretch, Pin/Unpin, Mark Seam); the islands then overlap each other in the layout.
tool: UV editor > UV > Average Islands Scale
view: legs and feet front view, UV editor showing overlapped islands
why: Equalise texel size after unwrapping; overlapping is accepted for now because layout comes later.

action: Selects the hand with L / Ctrl+L, mirrors the selection to the other side (status bar says 784 faces mirrored), presses U and picks Unwrap Minimum Stretch; the whole body then shows a more even grid texture.
tool: Edit Mode, Ctrl+L, Shift+Ctrl+M (Select Mirror), U > Unwrap Minimum Stretch
view: three-quarter view of the arm and hand with the checker; Alt+Z toggles X-ray while selecting
why: Fix the finger stretching on both hands at once.

action: Selects the front torso with L, presses U > Minimum Stretch, then UV > Average Islands Scale from the menu; the chest island moves to a new spot in the UV editor and the checker on the chest looks even.
tool: U > Unwrap Minimum Stretch; UV > Average Islands Scale
view: front and back view of the torso with the checker
why: Same fix as the feet applied island by island, then equalise.

action: With the UV-editor islands collapsing on top of each other (orange), runs Average Islands Scale again, then selects the head with L, presses U and hovers Unwrap Minimum Stretch to unwrap the head.
tool: Average Islands Scale; U menu on the head
view: front of the head and neck with seam lines
why: Minimum Stretch is the method used throughout; the head island is next.

action: Notes stretching on mouth and nose in the checker view, selects the head island, centres it in the UV editor by moving (G) it onto an empty part of the grid (header reads about Dx 0.85 Dy 0.02); the head island appears as a flat face with eyes, nostrils and mouth.
view: front close-up of the face, UV editor zoomed to the head island
why: Work on the face alone in free space so pinned edits do not collide with other islands.
reader_equivalent: edit([body]) with a face-only selection; flatten_uv(body, ...)

action: Zoomed into the mouth opening in the UV editor with the stretch overlay: pins the border, selects the lower lip edge loop and moves it down along Y (header D -0.0003 along Y), watching the yellow tips at both mouth corners.
tool: UV editor, P pin, G move along Y
view: UV editor face zoom; Stretch overlay on
why: Close the mouth gap in UV space so lip squares stop stretching.
reader_equivalent: flatten_uv(body, lambda p: <lip row test>, factor=0.0, axis=1)

action: Scales the mouth rows to a line along Y (header Scale 0.5196 along Y), then moves the row above the lips down with G and watches the 3D face texture change; the checker squares on the lips tighten.
tool: UV editor, S then Y, G
view: UV editor zoomed on the lips beside the 3D face front view (Ctrl+Space used to resize)
why: Match the lip squares to the cheeks; the 3D view shows the result live because Live Unwrap is on.
reader_equivalent: flatten_uv(body, <lip-row test>, factor=0.5, axis=1) then uv.minimize_stretch

action: Presses G then Y to move rows of the lip UVs down in small steps (headers D -0.0006 and D -0.0030 along Y) and undoes once with Ctrl+Z when the result stretches, checking the face texture each time.
view: split: UV editor close-up and face close-up in the 3D view
why: Refine lip shapes row by row until the lettered squares on the mouth match the face.
reader_equivalent: flatten_uv(...) then clear_pins and re-check uv_report stretch_p95

action: Box-selects rings of UVs around the mouth corners with Shift and drag, presses P to pin them (they show red), repeating around the other corner and around the lower lip so the mouth shape is fixed.
tool: UV editor, box select, P pin
view: UV editor zoomed on the mouth next to the 3D face
why: Pins hold the good parts so grab edits elsewhere only move what is free.
reader_equivalent: set l[uv].pin_uv = True on the chosen loops (as in flatten_uv)

action: Shift-click picks more mouth rows to pin, then selects the Grab tool in the UV editor toolbar (tooltip Grab UVs) and enlarges the brush with F, a circle of size about 318 appears over the face.
tool: UV editor > Grab UVs tool, F to change size
view: UV editor, mouth zoom with pinned vertices as red dots
why: Move groups of UVs smoothly instead of one at a time.
reader_equivalent: no brush; write UV positions for the chosen loops and relax with bpy.ops.uv.minimize_stretch

action: With Grab UVs active (header Size 92 px, then 228 px; Strength 1.000; Falloff; Drag: Select Box) drags pinned-free UVs around the lower lip and the nose; sets brush size with F between strokes and checks the face on the 3D view.

settings.falloff: shown in header, preset not legible

view: UV editor face zoom beside the 3D face turning to the side
why: Even out the lip and nose squares.
reader_equivalent: manual UV edit: nudge selected loops with l[uv].uv += offset, pin, then uv.minimize_stretch(iterations=200)

action: Box-selects the UVs around the nose, pins them with P, goes back to the Grab brush and drags with sizes about 210 and 330 px, undoing with Ctrl+Z, until the nose cells match the cheeks.
tool: UV editor box select, P, Grab UVs tool
view: UV editor nose zoom, 3D face from the front
why: Same-size squares on the nose as on the rest of the face.
reader_equivalent: manual UV push of nose loops plus pin and uv.minimize_stretch

action: Shows the face island in the UV editor with the eye sockets as holes; says that unwrapping Angle Based leaves other parts unchanged, then undoes with Ctrl+Z; looks at the eyelids in the 3D view and checks them in close-up.
tool: U > Unwrap Angle Based tried, Ctrl+Z; Grab UVs (size 144 px)
view: UV editor face island next to a three-quarter 3D face view
why: Test whether another method would help, then keep the earlier result; the eyes close so the lids matter.
reader_equivalent: keep Minimum Stretch; use flatten_uv on the eye-opening rows

action: Brings the face UV in to a flat eye slit on each side (both eye openings squeezed to a line), then brushes around the nose with Grab (size 144 px, then 82 px) before ending the face work; no mirroring of the face UVs is done.
tool: UV editor, Scale Y and Grab UVs
view: UV editor face zoom with the eyes and nose visible
why: The eyes will close, so the lid UVs are flat; the face is declared finished.
reader_equivalent: flatten_uv(body, lambda p: <eye-opening rows>, factor=0.0, pin=True); clear_pins(body)

action: Moves the face island into the UV square and enlarges it.
view: maximized UV Editor with stretch colors
why: Reserve more texture space for the face.

action: Compares the resized face island with the checker on the character.
view: front-oriented checker view beside UV layout
why: Show that increasing UV area makes the checker markings smaller on the face.

action: Places the enlarged face near the top of the square and identifies an arm island on the model.
view: UV layout and front-oriented character
why: Build a recognizable layout organized by body part.
reader_equivalent: select corresponding mesh faces and transform their UV coordinates with bmesh

action: Moves and rotates the two arm islands to opposite sides of the face island.
tool: UV Editor linked selection, move and rotate
view: UV layout and front-oriented checker model
why: Keep corresponding body parts on their respective sides of the layout.
reader_equivalent: transform each arm island's UV coordinates with bmesh

action: Brings the leg islands together below the face and examines their adjacent boundaries.
tool: UV Editor linked selection and move
view: UV Editor close-up and oblique checker model
why: Arrange the legs while avoiding island intersections.
reader_equivalent: transform leg islands with bmesh; check uv_overlap_faces

action: Repositions the paired leg islands side by side in the lower part of the square.
tool: UV Editor linked selection and move
view: UV Editor and checker-covered legs
why: Give the leg islands a clear, separated placement.

action: Selects the neck on the model to identify its UV island among the remaining pieces.
tool: 3D viewport linked selection and UV Editor
view: front close-up of neck beside UV layout
why: Disambiguate the neck island before placing it.
reader_equivalent: identify the neck faces by mesh position and inspect their UV loops

action: Selects an ear on the model, then rotates, enlarges and places its island near the face.
tool: UV Editor move, rotate and scale
view: front and rear head close-ups with UV layout
why: Place ear pieces near the face and give the visible ear additional texture space.
reader_equivalent: scale_islands and transform ear UV coordinates with bmesh

action: Selects the feet and shrinks their UV pieces before placing them in spare space.
view: front-oriented feet and maximized UV layout
why: Spend less texture area on feet covered by footwear.
reader_equivalent: scale_islands on complete foot islands followed by pack

action: Reduces and repositions sole-shaped islands, then adjusts nearby torso and leg islands.
tool: UV Editor linked selection, scale and move
view: UV Editor close-up and checker-covered feet
why: Fit lower-priority foot surfaces around the larger body pieces.
reader_equivalent: scale_islands and transform selected UV islands with bmesh

action: Adjusts and scales the two leg islands while separating their edges from neighboring islands.
view: UV Editor close-up beside checker feet
why: Prevent intersections while fitting the body layout.

action: Moves and rotates small finger-shaped UV islands into the hand group.
view: maximized UV Editor
why: Group related small islands so they remain identifiable.
reader_equivalent: transform individual island UV coordinates with bmesh

action: Identifies a finger on the model and aligns its island with neighboring finger pieces.
tool: linked selection and UV Editor rotate and move
view: hand close-up alongside UV layout
why: Keep the finger pieces grouped and similarly oriented.
reader_equivalent: identify corresponding faces and transform island UVs with bmesh

action: Places the remaining underside finger islands in a row beside the hand pieces.
tool: linked selection and UV Editor move and rotate
view: underside of hand and maximized UV close-up
why: Keep the palm-side finger pieces ordered and easy to find.
reader_equivalent: transform individual finger island UVs with bmesh

action: Reviews one hand group and starts moving the opposite hand's islands into place.
tool: UV Editor linked selection and move
view: maximized UV Editor
why: Organize the second hand separately from the first.
reader_equivalent: transform opposite-hand island UVs with bmesh

action: Moves the little-finger and thumb pieces into the second hand's group.
tool: linked selection and UV Editor move and rotate
view: hand close-up beside UV layout
why: Complete an ordered group for the other hand.
reader_equivalent: transform individual hand island UVs with bmesh

action: Repositions the final thumb piece and adjusts neighboring hand islands.
view: UV layout and hand close-up
why: Keep small hand pieces arranged without crowding.
reader_equivalent: transform island UVs with bmesh; check uv_overlap_faces

action: Reviews the completed body UV layout and reveals the clothed character for the next object.
view: full UV square beside front-oriented character
why: Finish the body pass before starting clothing.
reader_equivalent: inspect exported UV layout and change object visibility with bpy

action: Enters shirt Edit Mode and selects edges around the sleeve and shoulder region.
tool: UV Editing workspace and mesh edge selection
view: front and oblique close-ups of shirt topology
why: Use the garment's construction lines to guide seam placement.

action: Orbits beneath the shirt and selects the side edge as it reaches the inward-turned hem.
tool: 3D viewport edge selection and UV Editor
view: underside and side close-ups of shirt hem
why: Inspect how the interior rim connects to the shirt panel.
reader_equivalent: inspect shirt topology and mark seam_path on intended side edges

action: Assigns the existing checker material to the unwrapped shirt and inspects the result.
view: isolated shirt in 3D beside stretch-colored UV islands

action: Places the shirt front and back side by side and rotates and moves sleeve islands underneath.

view: maximized UV Editor
why: Give the shirt a readable manually organized layout.

action: Inspects the finished shirt checker, selects the skirt and assigns the checker material.

view: oblique and underside skirt close-ups beside UV Editor
why: Separate the interior rim region for unwrapping.

action: Marks a skirt panel edge and mirrors the selection to the opposite side.

action: Selects a vertical edge path up a skirt pleat, marks it and repeats on the mirrored side.
view: close-up of checker-covered pleat and UV layout
why: Split the folded panel where the checker is distorted.

action: Finishes a mirrored seam, inspects the exterior checker, then reveals the hidden skirt interior.

action: Examines the inside skirt checker and selects an additional path near the lower lining.

view: maximized underside skirt close-up

why: Reduce distortion symmetrically on the lining.

action: Rotates and places narrow triangular skirt islands beside the main panels.

action: Inspects the separated toe island and reveals the other shoe pieces.
